summary: Iron Mountain in Bartlett: a 1939 notice listed a tower under construction or planned; NH lists say it is gone; no source describes the summit today.

facts.status_note: No longer standing, per the Forest Fire Lookout Association list and a hiking list.

events.note: August 3, 1939 Portsmouth Herald item lists a tower under construction or planned on Iron, 2,727, in Bartlett. Completion is not stated.

evidence.supports: Dated 3 Aug 1939 notice credited to the Portsmouth Herald: towers under construction or planned, Iron at 2,727, Bartlett
evidence.quote: August 3, 1939: "Towers, either under construction or planned, are to be situated on the following: Iron, 2,727, Bartlett, by Camp Swift River of Albany." (The Portsmouth Herald)
Mountains which Once Had a Fire Tower

evidence.supports: No longer standing, artifacts noted; elevation 2,716
evidence.quote: Iron Mountain - Bartlett 2716 No Longer Standing / Artifacts

sources.title: You Are Here: NH Fire Towers

notes_for_editor: Only one dated item: the 1939 notice of a tower under construction or planned. No readable source confirms it was finished, so no built date is stated. The brief's access 'unknown' stands; no source gives access. Not used because they could not be read: onlyinyourstate.com (403 here) reportedly dates a tower to 1942-1948 and describes footings on the summit; a 1928 Facebook photo post (New Hampshire-then and now) says the mountain was home to a tower; the NHDFL history PDF returned 403 and its Wayback copy did not load. Verify the 1942-1948 claim before adding it. Heights differ across lists (2,716, 2,726, 2,727 ft); the story says so.
